text:
Kailer Yamamoto has been one of the quietly best players in Utah this season. Through 15 games he has 12 points, and at 5v5 the Mammoth get 64% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 9 points better than when he's off. He's scoring 2.98 points per 60.

The goals haven't followed. He's gone eight games without one on 2.6 expected goals, and has 3 for the season on 5.5 expected. That's the kind of gap that tends to close: he keeps getting the looks. In the meantime he's passing, including a three-assist night against San Jose, which the team's video summed up as "the patience of Kailer Yamamoto."

None of this is new. Evolving-Hockey had him 53rd among 401 forwards last season at 2.0 wins above replacement, with a defensive impact in the 98th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 84th percentile for primary shot assists. His ice time is up more than two minutes a night lately. Utah seems to have noticed.
headline: Yamamoto is driving play, goals pending
